svg.title: Proof. The score effect is Ah,e = (1 −e)E−h −eEh, whose spectral range lies within [−e, 1 −e]. Each probe-preparation error changes its expectation by at most δprep, and future source deviation changes it by at most δS,h. Its drift is at most (1 −e)d−h + edh by operator-norm duality. Combine with Eq. (71) and average probe ages to prove Eq. (72). The conclusive effect E+ + E−lies between zero and identity, so its preparation/source deviations cost the same trace-distance margins, and its drift costs Dw + Dc. The C counter proves Eq. (73). Positivity of that rate lower bound ensures bCh + Dw −Dc > 0. Setting the right side of Eq. (72) to zero then gives exactly Eq. (74). Its threshold can be selected from the data because the coverage event is uniform over e. Every statement is about the nominated label marginal and holds for any inert-reference extension of that input marginal. It is not equality of reference assemblages or of complete quantum instruments.
